parts.label: a
parts.technique: Mode from stem-and-leaf
parts.reason: Finding the mode of a data set is covered by S2.3 (measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Quartiles from stem-and-leaf/grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers measures of variation including interpercentile ranges and use of linear interpolation to find percentiles, which covers quartiles.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Mean and standard deviation from summary statistics (Sxx)
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly allows calculation of standard deviation from summary statistics using Sxx formula.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Pearson's measure of skewness
parts.reason: No statement mentions skewness or a skewness coefficient; this named concept is absent from the specification statements, so it is out despite using otherwise in-spec quantities (mean, mode, sd).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Reasons for negative skewness (mean<median<mode, quartile spacing)
parts.reason: Depends on the skewness concept from part (d) which is not covered by any statement; also comparing quartile spacing as evidence of skew is not an explicit statement topic.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Forming equations using E(X) of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean of discrete random variables; forming an equation using E(X)=3.5 requires this excluded concept.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solve simultaneous equations from (a) for p, q
parts.reason: This part only makes sense using the equations from part (a), which relies on the excluded E(X) calculation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Variance of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of variance of discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Var(3-2X) using linear transformation of variance
parts.reason: Depends directly on Var(X) found in the excluded part (c).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Draw scatter diagram
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly covers interpreting scatter diagrams for bivariate data; drawing one from raw data is the same topic and skill.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Justify linear regression model from scatter pattern
parts.reason: This is a qualitative judgement about the scatter diagram (points lying close to a line), not a calculation involving a regression line, so it falls under S2.2's coverage of scatter diagrams/correlation rather than the excluded calculation.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculate a and b for regression line y=a+bx
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes 'calculations involving regression lines'.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Interpret gradient b of regression line
parts.reason: Depends on the value of b calculated in the excluded part (c), and is itself a regression-line calculation interpretation excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Predict y using regression equation
parts.reason: Requires substituting into the regression equation from the excluded part (c).

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Comment on reliability of regression predictions (interpolation/extrapolation)
parts.reason: Although interpolation/extrapolation concepts appear in S2.2, this part only makes sense after using the excluded regression predictions from part (e).

parts.label: tree diagram
parts.technique: Tree diagram for sampling without replacement
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly mentions use of tree diagrams for conditional probability.

parts.label: (a) P(second red)
parts.technique: Total probability using tree diagram
parts.reason: Uses standard conditional/total probability techniques covered by S3.2.

parts.label: (b) P(both red | second red)
parts.technique: Conditional probability formula
parts.reason: Directly matches S3.2's conditional probability formula P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Reasons for using statistical models
parts.reason: S3.3 explicitly covers modelling with probability including critiquing/reasoning about models.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Examples of normal and discrete uniform distributions
parts.reason: S4.2 covers Normal distribution as a model and S4.1 explicitly requires students to identify the discrete uniform distribution.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Venn diagram for two events
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly mentions use of Venn diagrams for conditional probability topics.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Find P(A), P(B) from Venn diagram
parts.reason: Basic probability manipulation covered by S3.2 guidance (P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A∩B) etc).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability P(A|B)
parts.reason: Matches S3.2's explicit conditional probability formula.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Test for independence of events
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers use of P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) to test independence.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: Same as (a), standard Normal probability calculation covered by S4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Independent events probability with Normal distributions
parts.reason: Combines S3.1 (independent events) with S4.2 (Normal probabilities), both explicitly in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Critique independence assumption
parts.reason: S3.3 explicitly covers critiquing modelling assumptions such as independence.
